---
title: "Findings"
subtitle: "What we learned, and what it means for Admissions"
---
## How Well Could We Actually Predict Enrollment Destination?
We tested three models. All performed similarly, correctly predicting a
student's destination category **around 43–45% of the time**. This represents a meaningful improvement over random guessing across four categories, but far from perfect.

| Model | Overall Accuracy | Notes |
|-------|---------|----------------|
| Multinomial Logistic Regression | 43% | Best at identifying Local Public and Three Large Public enrollees; struggled most with Local Private |
| Support Vector Machine | 45% | Best at identifying Local Private enrollees; struggled most with NW5 |
| XGBoost | 43% | Most balanced across categories; best precision for NW5 |

Since XGBoost was the most balanced across categories and is well-suited to handling missing data (which applicant data has a lot of), we focused on it for finetuning and looking into its performance in more detail.

The model found that overall, **region of origin was the single strongest predictor for every destination category.** After region, the next most influential factors varied by destination:

| Destination Category | 2nd Most Influential | 3rd Most Influential | 4th Most Influential |
|---|---|---|---|
| NW5 | SAT/ACT Superscore | First-Generation Status | Days to Application Submission |
| Local Private | Student Athlete Status | Weighted GPA | Curriculum Rating |
| Three Large Public | Student Athlete Status | EFC/SAI (Financial Need) | — |
| Local Public | Days to Application Submission | Admission Plan | — |

The regions that impacted the classification in each category the most were widely varied across categories. For Local Private schools, an applicant being from California meant a higher likelihood of attending, while for a Local Public school, an applicant being from California meant a much lower likelihood of attending. For Northwest 5 schools, applicants from California, states other than Washington and Oregon, and the Bellingham area of Washington are more likely to attend. 

![Feature Importance for Northwest 5 School Destination.](/images/nw5_shap_beeswarm.png)

![Impact of Applicant Region of Origin for Northwest 5 School Destination.](/images/nw5_shap_cat_plot.png)

Additional features and destination categories are explored in the [full writeup](deliverables.qmd).


## The Big Picture

No model can say with certainty where a specific student will enroll. But
across every approach we tried, a few clear and consistent patterns emerged
about *what* tends to influence a student's choice. Using an applicant's region of origin, overall academic profile, and any financial information, one can gain a general understanding of where a student might enroll.

We found that destination depends on a specific *combination* of actors rather than a single broad "type" of student. Even if these predictions cannot be trusted to fully predict where a student will enroll, they can still provide some insight into how to attract them to Willamette. Since the models do not have an extremely high precision or recall rate, entire marketing and enrollment strategies should not be based on these results.

## Limitations

- This analysis is specific to Willamette's applicant pool and competitive
  set; the findings may not generalize to other institutions.
- Only three years of data and roughly 6,500 confirmed outcomes were
  available, which limits statistical power, especially for smaller
  destination categories.
- Specific financial details (beyond fee waivers, need-based aid, and
  FAFSA/EFC data) were excluded to protect student privacy, which may limit
  our ability to explain financially driven decisions.
- These results describe *associations*, not causes. They can help target
  outreach, but they don't explain *why* any individual student chooses one
  school over another.

## Future Work

More analysis could be completed on the interactions between features as they pertain to the enrollment destination. This would allow for more actionable results, as it would be easier to categorize students.
The creation of an interactive model or function that would allow the Admissions and Enrollment team to insert a student's data and receive and predicted destination category would be extremely beneficial.

To increase the robustness and accuracy of the model, there are a few directions that could be followed, including an increased sample size and the use of alternative modeling methods. Potential methods include Neural Networks and Naive Bayes.
